name: FDC - Desarrollo y Escritura de Largometraje (Fondo para el Desarrollo Cinematográfico, Proimágenes Colombia)
amount: Varies by modality (writing vs. development); exact 2026 caps not confirmed in public summary — check official convocatoria bases
deadline: 2026 Phase 2 (Desarrollo, Escritura, Formación) closed April 12, 2026; recurring annual, opens ~Jan-Feb each year
requirements: Open only to Colombian individuals and Colombian legal entities; project must compete in the specific modality matching its stage (script writing or development)
previousWinners: Full results published annually at convocatoriafdc.com
strategy: Colombia's flagship state cinema fund; screenplay/development modalities are less competitive than production and are a strong entry point for first/second features by Colombian filmmakers.
applicationFee: Free to apply

name: Programa Ibermedia - Codesarrollo y Coproducción Iberoamericana (Colombia)
amount: Coproduction loans up to $150,000 USD (fiction) / $100,000 USD (documentary) per project; codevelopment amounts smaller and vary by modality
deadline: 2026 convocatoria open through March 30, 2026 (annual, opens ~late Jan each year)
requirements: Applicant must be an independent production company registered in a Program Ibermedia member country (Colombia is a founding member); project must be a co-production/co-development with a company from another member country
previousWinners: Annual grantee lists published at programaibermedia.com
strategy: Colombia is one of Ibermedia's most active member countries; best suited to producer-driven applications that already have an international co-production partner attached.
applicationFee: Not specified — verify on official page

name: IDFA Bertha Fund - Production & Post-Production Grant (Colombia)
amount: Up to €25,000 (Classic grant); Europe Minority Co-production Scheme up to €40,000
deadline: Two rounds annually; 2026 first-round deadline (Feb 10) has closed — next round to be announced on professionals.idfa.nl
requirements: Director (and ideally producer) must be from and currently living/working in a country on the IBF Classic Country List; Colombia is an eligible country; creative documentary in production or post-production
previousWinners: Grantee lists published each round at professionals.idfa.nl
strategy: Favors author-driven, formally ambitious nonfiction; consistent track record of supporting Colombian documentary directors, including first/second features.
applicationFee: Not specified — verify on official page

name: Beca de Creación de Cortometraje de Ficción — Nuevas Directoras o Directores (IDARTES / Cinemateca de Bogotá)
amount: $45,000,000 COP fund pool for the modality (~$11,000 USD at mid-2026 rates; per-project amount depends on number of winners selected)
deadline: 2026 cycle closed March 26, 2026; recurring annual (Portafolio Distrital de Estímulos, opens ~Jan-Feb each year)
requirements: Directed by a new (emerging) director; Bogotá-based creators prioritized under the district stimulus portfolio; project proposal and prior work sample
previousWinners: Full results published annually at sicon.scrd.gov.co
strategy: Explicitly favors new/emerging directors over established ones — a strong first-short fit for an MFA student with ties to Bogotá; companion documentary-short version also runs annually.
applicationFee: Free to apply

name: Beca de Creación de Cortometraje Documental — Nuevas Directoras o Directores (IDARTES / Cinemateca de Bogotá)
amount: $45,000,000 COP fund pool for the modality (~$11,000 USD at mid-2026 rates; per-project amount depends on number of winners selected)
deadline: 2026 cycle closed April 6, 2026; recurring annual (Portafolio Distrital de Estímulos, opens ~Jan-Feb each year)
requirements: Directed by a new (emerging) director; Bogotá-based creators prioritized under the district stimulus portfolio; project proposal and prior work sample
previousWinners: Full results published annually at sicon.scrd.gov.co
strategy: Sister program to the fiction-short new-directors beca; nonfiction MFA thesis projects with a Bogotá connection are a strong fit.
applicationFee: Free to apply

name: Telefilm Canada - Talent to Watch Program
amount: Up to $250,000 CAD (fiction); documentary/other streams vary
deadline: Multiple annual intakes across four streams (General, Indigenous, Black/People of Colour, Festival Selection); check telefilm.ca for current 2026 dates
requirements: First-time feature film director who is Canadian; Festival Selection stream requires a short film that screened at a recognized festival; key creative team members must be emerging talent
previousWinners: 17 film teams backed with $3.45M in a recent round — telefilm.ca
strategy: One of the most prominent first-feature launchpads in Canada; strongly favors historically underrepresented and emerging creators and closes permanently once a director has made a feature — a one-shot opportunity right out of an MFA program.
applicationFee: Free to apply

name: NFB Filmmaker Assistance Program (FAP)
amount: In-kind post-production services: up to $7,500 value per filmmaker (short films) / $15,000 (features); NFB covers 90-100% of cost depending on filmmaker's distance from Montreal
deadline: Annual intake opens January 30; recurring yearly
requirements: Independent Canadian filmmaker (anglophone program); project in post-production; filmmaker retains full copyright
previousWinners: Cohort lists published each cycle at production.nfbonf.ca
strategy: Not cash — an in-kind post-production subsidy at NFB's Montreal facilities (or local reimbursement); valuable for finishing an MFA thesis short with minimal cash outlay.
applicationFee: Free to apply

name: Hot Docs-Slaight Family Fund
amount: $15,000-$60,000 CAD (3-5 projects funded annually)
deadline: Annual call; check hotdocs.ca/industry/film-funds for current 2026-27 dates
requirements: Music-themed documentary (Canadian music's role in the world, or international music stories told by Canadian filmmakers); applicant corporation must be primary rights holder and have a prior commercially released or broadcast credit — not a first-project grant
previousWinners: $145,000 awarded to five Canadian projects in a recent cycle — hotdocs.ca
strategy: Niche but well-funded music-documentary fund; note the prior-credit requirement means it suits filmmakers with at least one prior release, not a pure student-first-film grant.
applicationFee: Not specified — verify on official page

name: Crazy8s Film Society - Crazy8s Short Film Challenge (Vancouver)
amount: $2,000 CAD cash plus mentorship and a full production/post-production package per selected team
deadline: Annual pitch call; 2026 program listed at crazy8s.film/programs/crazy8s-2026 — check site for current dates
requirements: BC-based emerging/mid-career filmmaker with limited access to resources; pitch an 8-12 minute short to a jury of film professionals; 6 teams selected; film shot within an 8-day window
previousWinners: 151 short films produced since 1999, many festival award winners — crazy8s.film
strategy: A fast, resource-light way to make a fully-crewed short with mentorship; strong community reputation in the BC/Vancouver industry, useful for building local connections post-MFA.
applicationFee: Not specified — verify on official page

name: Ontario Creates IP Fund - Linear Content Stream (Development)
amount: Development stage funding amount varies by project; Production stage up to 30% of Ontario spend, capped at $200,000 CAD
deadline: Multiple annual deadlines; next listed intake Sept 22, 2026 (check current cycle at ontariocreates.ca)
requirements: Applicant must be a Canadian-owned production company incorporated in Ontario or federally with Ontario registration and a principal place of business in Ontario; sole proprietors must incorporate to qualify
previousWinners: Not publicly itemized per-project; program guidelines at ontariocreates.ca
strategy: Replaced the former Ontario Creates Film Fund in 2025; best suited to graduates who incorporate a production company in Ontario after their MFA rather than individual student applicants.
applicationFee: Not specified — verify on official page

name: Arts Council England - National Lottery Project Grants
deadline: Always open / rolling - no fixed deadline, apply for either 'up to £30,000' (12-week decision) or 'over £30,000' (14-week decision) tier
requirements: Applicant (individual practitioner or organisation) must be based in (live in or have a business address in) England or the wider UK, and must have a UK bank account in the name of the applicant. Open access programme, not film-specific - project must have a clear public benefit.
previousWinners: Not centrally listed for film; searchable via Arts Council England's Project Grants data tool
strategy: Frame the film project around public benefit/artistic merit rather than commercial return; useful for artist-filmmakers, experimental/hybrid work, and projects that don't fit standard industry film funds. Apply for the lower (£30k or under) tier for faster turnaround.
applicationFee: Free

name: Screen Scotland / TAKE THREE - North Star Shorts
amount: £25,000 production + £3,000 development support per film
deadline: Annual - 2026 round closed 19 June 2026; recurring annual scheme, check TAKE THREE site for next opening
requirements: Applicant must be resident in Scotland (proof of address required if selected); early-career talent; live action or animation fiction shorts up to 15 minutes; must be UK Film Tax Relief eligible; team should include writer, director/animator and producer (individual writers may apply without a full team).
previousWinners: Six films funded per annual round; individual titles not consolidated publicly
strategy: Best for Scotland-resident (or relocating) MFA grads with a tight, producible 15-minute concept; delivered via TAKE THREE with Screen Scotland and BFI NETWORK backing.
applicationFee: Free

name: Screen Scotland / TAKE THREE - The Bigger Picture
amount: Not publicly disclosed per-film (funds up to 4 shorts per round, including one in Gaelic)
deadline: Annual - 2026 round deadline 5 June 2026; recurring annual scheme, check TAKE THREE site for next opening
requirements: Scotland-based filmmakers only; aimed at creatively ambitious, high-value shorts intended to bridge the gap toward a first feature; delivered through TAKE THREE with Screen Scotland and BFI NETWORK support.
strategy: Position the short explicitly as a proof-of-concept or calling-card for a first feature; strong fit for Scotland-based MFA grads planning a feature next.
applicationFee: Free

name: Northern Ireland Screen - New Shorts Focus
amount: Up to £12,500 production award (following a development phase); exact amount not publicly fixed for every round
deadline: Recurring annual scheme (2024/25 round ran Oct 2025-Mar 2026); check Northern Ireland Screen site for next call
requirements: Northern Ireland resident writer or writer/director from an under-represented background, with at least one independently made or funded short-film-level writing/directing credit; six-month writer-led development process with a development producer, after which up to three projects may receive a production award, contingent on attaching an NI-resident production company.
strategy: Targeted at under-represented NI-resident emerging writers/writer-directors; apply with a distinctive fiction short concept and be prepared to attach a local production company for the production stage.
applicationFee: Free

name: BFI National Lottery Discovery Feature Funding
amount: Typically £500,000 - £850,000, up to £1,000,000 maximum
deadline: Rolling rounds; Round 2 closed 13 Aug 2026, Round 3 opens 12 Nov 2026 and closes 16 Dec 2026
requirements: For debut directors on features with production budgets of £1,000,000-£3,500,000 (director cannot have previously directed a feature at/above £1M budget or with commercial UK/Irish distribution; self-distributed features and documentary features don't disqualify debut status). Must apply at least 20 weeks before first day of principal photography. Project must address at least three BFI funding aims (e.g. EDI, UK-wide talent, environmental sustainability).
previousWinners: Not consolidated on this page; check BFI's funded projects announcements
strategy: Aimed at MFA grads with a UK first-feature project ready to move to production; build the budget and EDI/talent case explicitly around BFI's stated funding aims.
applicationFee: Free

name: CNC / Institut français - Aide aux cinémas du monde (ACM)
amount: Up to €300,000 before production (up to €500,000 for French-initiated projects with budgets ≥€2.5M); up to €70,000 after production
deadline: Multiple 2026 sessions - before production: 2 Mar, 2 Jun, 2 Sep, 23 Nov 2026; after production: 9 Feb, 13 Apr, 4 Sep, 9 Nov 2026
requirements: Selective aid, co-managed by CNC and Institut français, for feature-length fiction/animation/documentary international co-productions with first theatrical release intended in France. Applicant must be a production company established in France; director must be a foreign national (or a French director whose film is not originally in French). Foreign directors/producers participate via a French co-producer.
previousWinners: Numerous international festival titles historically supported; full list on CNC site
strategy: Not directly applicable to a solo MFA grad without a French co-producer - most useful once you have identified or are seeking a French production partner for a first feature international co-production.
applicationFee: Free

name: Fondation Gan pour le Cinéma - Aide à la Création
amount: €53,000 per project (€3,000 to the director, €50,000 to the producer)
deadline: Annual call - check 'Devenir Lauréat' page for exact 2026/2027 submission window (recurring annual)
requirements: Supports 4 first or second fiction feature film projects per year (screenplay-stage submissions), plus 1 Special Prize; does not fund short films. Submitted via a French production company; nationality/residency requirements not fully detailed on the public page - confirm directly with the Foundation.
previousWinners: Past laureates include films such as Divines; full list on Fondation Gan site
strategy: Relevant once an MFA grad has a first-feature screenplay and a French (or French-affiliated) producer attached; strong prestige credential (35+ year track record) alongside the cash award.
applicationFee: Free

name: Cinéfondation - Résidence (Festival de Cannes)
amount: Fully-funded Paris residence (housing + program); stipend amount not publicly disclosed
deadline: Applications for the session running 15 Mar-31 Jul 2027 close 30 September 2026 (two sessions per year, ~6 months apart)
requirements: Candidates must NOT be French residents or citizens; must have made one or more short films (or at most one feature); one of these prior works must have been selected at a major ('Category A') festival such as Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Toronto, Busan, San Sebastián, Locarno, Rotterdam, Sundance or Clermont-Ferrand; under 35 at session start; fluent in English or French; max 3 applications; must reside in Paris for the full ~4.5-month session working on a first or second fiction feature screenplay.
previousWinners: Alumni list published on Festival de Cannes / Cinéfondation site
strategy: A strong fit for non-French, festival-selected MFA grads developing a first feature - note the festival-selection prerequisite, which typically means a prior short needs to have played a top-tier festival first.
applicationFee: Not specified on public page - appears free

name: Fondation Beaumarchais-SACD - Bourse d'écriture Cinéma court métrage
amount: €2,000 net per project (8-10 grants awarded per year)
deadline: Annual - 2026 deadline 9 June 2026 at 7pm; results announced December 2026
requirements: For 'emerging' authors (no more than one previously professionally produced fiction short); screenplay must be written and shot in French; original fiction only (no adaptations or documentaries), 5-30 minutes; applicant must apply directly (not via a producer) and must have either audiovisual/film training or a production company attached; no nationality/residency restriction, but the film must be in French.
previousWinners: Not consolidated publicly; ~8-10 laureates per year
strategy: Viable for MFA grads writing/directing a French-language short, even without French citizenship - the binding constraint is the French-language requirement, not nationality.
applicationFee: Free

name: ARTE France - Unité Cinéma / Court-circuit (Short Film Acquisition, Pre-purchase & Co-production)
amount: Acquisition: ~€600/minute (18-month exclusivity); fiction pre-purchase: ~€1,200/film; co-production terms vary by project (animation up to 30 min)
deadline: No fixed application deadline - ongoing direct submission to ARTE's Unité Cinéma (Court-circuit strand)
requirements: Not a traditional open-call grant with a set deadline - ARTE's Court-circuit team acquires, pre-purchases or co-produces roughly 30 short/medium-length films per year (up to ~30 minutes) for broadcast on Court-circuit and arte.tv. Typically approached through a French producer or directly via ARTE's Cinema Unit contact.
previousWinners: Not publicly consolidated; broadcast history visible on arte.tv/court-circuit
strategy: Best approached once a short is finished or in post, ideally with a French producer/sales relationship - useful as a broadcast/distribution and finishing-funds route rather than a production grant to apply for from scratch.
applicationFee: Free
